meta.title: Endless Entrainment Normalize Build
meta.author: Grex
meta.summary: Give the boss Normalize through Entrainment so its attacks cannot hurt you, then whittle it down. Compact four-slot team built from fusions.
meta.credits: Thanks in the guide to sang, Ellie, Pepo, Monkee, excoman. Recommended tools: Triickstr's Team Planner and Sandstorm's Dex.

pros: Little to no egg move investment
Can farm Master Balls at any time
Regigigas carries for a long stretch
Almost never fails a shiny catch
Four team slots, no wasted abilities

cons.text: Needs hidden abilities, mainly Teddiursa and Regigigas

cons: Needs a wild Mat Block user

starters.name: Teddiursa
starters.role: Keeps Run Away as passive after fusion. Honey Gather speeds up rerolls. Learns Thief or Covet, and Roar, by TM.

starters.name: Pumpkaboo (Average)
starters.role: Illuminate works as a lure. Owns Trick-or-Treat, which pairs with Normalize. Frisk shows wild abilities without catching.

starters.name: Smoochum
starters.role: Fast, fuses later with the Normalize Pokémon. Emergency carry. Must bring Powder Snow so Smeargle can sketch it for the first fusion.

starters.name: Yamask
starters.role: Late game boss killer using damage over time. Has Heal Block from level 1. Staying unevolved keeps HP low so Leech Seed heals to full. Pichu and Diglett come with Sturdy as passive.

starters.name: Nincada
starters.role: Source of Shedinja, the boss killer. See the Nincada setup step in Splicing.

starters.name: Regigigas
starters.role: Centre of the build and a strong carry. Rock Slide is its best double battle move. Land's Wrath egg move replaces hunting for Rock Slide.

starters.name: Kyogre
starters.role: Carries the run with Endure, Ice Beam, Water Pulse and Water Spout. Later fuses with Skitty and becomes Killer Support. Kyogre stays the base, so the fusion keeps Mold Breaker as passive.

starters.name: Skitty
starters.role: Fusion partner for Kyogre. Learns Entrainment, Gastro Acid, Curse and Shed Tail through splicing, so Kyogre keeps its carry moves until the final fusion. As the second species it gives the fusion its Normalize ability. Kyogre + Skitty is Water/Normal.

starters.name: Smeargle
alternatives: Espurr (all have the Dark Void egg move)
starters.role: Sketch saves splicers. Its job is the first fusion onto Pumpkaboo, teaching Dark Void. Gastly, Drowzee, Lunatone and Espurr also have the Dark Void egg move and can do this instead, but only Smeargle brings Sketch, which saves 2 splicers for Staller.

items.name: Rock Slide TM
items.note: Not needed if Regigigas has Land's Wrath

items.name: Land's Wrath
items.note: Optional, does not count toward completion. Egg move, or splice it from a wild user. Having it also covers the Rock Slide TM.

items.name: Wide Lens
items.note: Nature's Madness is 90% accuracy. Two Wide Lens bring it to 100%.

items.name: Multi Lens
items.note: Two Multi Lens give Nature's Madness extra hits, which breaks more boss shields.

splicing.note: Always start with step 1, Smeargle onto Pumpkaboo. After that the order is up to you: Items, Splicing and Final fusions are all worked on at the same time, so do whatever is rarest or available in your current biome first. If you hold a pending target but find a rarer one (for example a Greninja for Mat Block), take the rarer one. Regigigas can hold on its own so you can stay in the carry phase longer.

steps.alt: Dark Void, Sketch and Powder Snow. Either works: Powder Snow comes from sketching Smoochum.

steps.partner: Wild Ruination or Nature's Madness user

steps.lock_note: Keeping this fusion locks Kyogre and shifts the run into the Running Phase.

steps.purpose: Evolve Nincada with an open party slot (party under 6) and a regular Poké Ball in the bag, not a Great Ball or better. Shedinja splits off with a copy of ALL held items, so move Soul Dews, Choice Scarfs and similar onto Nincada before it evolves.
Not needed. Gets Splicers out of the master pool.

final_builds.name: Staller
final_builds.rec: Hidden ability Midnight Lycanroc (No Guard), the fastest sand-immune No Guard pick

final_builds.name: Runner
final_builds.rec: Dugtrio, or hidden ability Midnight Lycanroc (No Guard)

final_builds.name: Killer Support
notes: Water/Normal. Before the fusion Kyogre carries with Endure, Ice Beam, Water Pulse and Water Spout.

final_builds.name: Boss Killer
notes: Threat: Slither Wing (Bug/Fighting, Scrappy passive) with Dual Wingbeat. Once Normalized, Dual Wingbeat hits Ghost through Scrappy, and its two hits get past Sturdy. Entrainment only replaces the active ability, so Slither Wing keeps Scrappy.

final_builds.name: Boss Killer
notes: Bug/Ghost. Wonder Guard: only super effective hits connect.
Nature's Madness, Conversion and Salt Cure come from move tutors. Heal Block is learned at level 41.
Wonder Guard is the counter to Slither Wing's Dual Wingbeat. Use Conversion with Nature's Madness in slot 1 first, so Shedinja is pure Fairy and Dual Wingbeat is no longer super effective.

spare_slots: Two team slots are free for luck. The guide strongly recommends a Mold Breaker Pokémon holding Gastro Acid, mainly for Gholdengo, if Teddiursa lacks Core Enforcer.

playbook.title: Standard boss
steps: Killer Support leads: Tera Ghost, then Entrainment on the boss so its attacks stop hitting.
Swap to Boss Killer and use its moves until the boss looks like it dies next turn, or each move has been used once.
Bring in Staller so Triple Lure is active and the next wave starts as a double battle.

playbook.title: Complicated boss (Slither Wing is the main counter)

steps.text: Use only Boss Killer and open with Leech Seed to heal to full each turn.
Shedinja's Wonder Guard counters Dual Wingbeat. Use Conversion first so it is pure Fairy and Dual Wingbeat cannot connect.

steps: When the boss is about to die, let it knock out one of your Pokémon so Staller enters safely.
If needed Staller can use Mat Block or Dark Void for a couple of turns.

playbook.title: Capturing safely
steps: Roar away the Pokémon you do not want.
Normalize the one you want to catch.
Throw regular balls. Ruination or Nature's Madness damages it, Dark Void puts it to sleep for better odds.
Slow but saves Master Balls. Works on bosses too.

playbook.title: Capturing on XX0 waves
steps: Use Trick-or-Treat on the target to make it Ghost type, immune to its partner's spread moves such as Discharge.
After Normalize, all your Pokémon become immune to both opponents within two turns, which cuts the stalling time a lot.

how_to_play.intro: First, Regigigas does all the fighting while you collect what your team needs. Then you switch to your final team, and most waves become quick double battles. You only really fight the bosses.

phases.title: Regigigas does the fighting
phases.when: Start of the run until step 17
points: Regigigas has the Normalize ability. It turns all of its moves into Normal moves and makes them stronger.
Its passive, Scrappy, lets Normal moves hit Ghost types too.
Give Regigigas every Silk Scarf you find. They make Normal moves stronger. This helps most at the start, so Regigigas can knock out enemies in one hit.
Rock Slide or Land's Wrath hits both enemies in a double battle. Darkest Lariat is for hitting one enemy.
Put Pumpkaboo second in your team. Its Illuminate passive brings more double battles. Keep one Lure going too, so normal waves are double battles.
The run can feel slow at first. It gets faster once you do the first fusion (Smeargle onto Pumpkaboo) and get the Lock Capsule.

phases.title: Kyogre does the fighting
phases.when: Start of the run until step 23
points: Kyogre carries with Endure, Ice Beam, Water Pulse and Water Spout.
Put Pumpkaboo second in your team. Its Illuminate passive brings more double battles. Keep one Lure going too, so normal waves are double battles.
The run can feel slow at first. It gets faster once you do the first fusion (Smeargle onto Pumpkaboo) and get the Lock Capsule.

phases.title: Collect everything
phases.when: At the same time as part 1
points: You work on Items, Splicing and Final fusions all at once.
Items are rewards, so take the ones you need whenever they show up, right from the first wave.
For splicing, always do the first fusion (Smeargle onto Pumpkaboo) first. After that, do whatever is rarest, or whatever you can find in the biome you are in.
When you get to a new biome, type its name in the I'm in box at the top. It shows what you can get there.

points.text: You only need Land's Wrath and Darkest Lariat in this part, while Regigigas is still doing the fighting.

phases.title: The big switch
points: Fuse Regigigas onto Jynx, teach it Entrainment, and keep them fused. This is Killer Support.
After this, Regigigas can't sweep with Normalize anymore. That's OK, because your new team takes over.
You could keep Land's Wrath on it, but the four Killer Support moves are more important.
If you do want to keep Land's Wrath, keep it when you fuse. After the fusion you can't get Regigigas's egg moves back, because Jynx is the main Pokémon and only Jynx's egg moves can be relearned.

phases.title: The big switch
points: Fuse Skitty onto Kyogre and keep them fused. This is Killer Support: Water/Normal, Normalize, passive Mold Breaker.
Its running moves are Entrainment, Gastro Acid, Shed Tail and Curse, spliced onto Skitty in steps 18 to 21, so Kyogre keeps carrying until this fusion.

phases.title: Running through waves
points: Staller and Runner take care of normal waves.

Lure abilities make double battles more likely. Staller and Runner each get one from their fusion (any lure ability: Illuminate, Arena Trap, No Guard or Commander), and Staller also has Illuminate as its passive.
Staller on its own is enough to make normal waves double battles. With both of them out you get three lures.

Double battle chance is worked out when the next battle is created: base 8 (32 when the next wave is a multiple of 10), divided by 4 for each lure effect (Lure items, plus each Pokémon on the field with a lure ability).

Waves ending in 0 skip the reward screen, so you can't swap before the next wave is created. That's why Staller goes out at the end of x50 waves. On other waves, swapping on the reward screen does count.
Sometimes you have to let one of your Pokémon faint so you can switch safely.
Bosses are for your boss team. See Standard boss and Complicated boss in In the run.
Only catch Pokémon the slow way when you are out of Master Balls. See Capturing safely. It's best to always get a new Master Ball after you use one, so you never run out.

optional_slot.title: Optional 5th slot: Prankster
optional_slot.note: A Prankster Pokémon with Tailwind and Psychic Terrain. 100% optional, it does not count toward completion.

move_order.note: Draft until Lucy or Grex confirm.

entries.text: Nature's Madness in slot 1. Conversion copies the type of the first move slot, so Shedinja becomes pure Fairy. That removes most weaknesses and keeps Wonder Guard useful.
